answer: Attention-Bonded Registration requires each new identity to accrue a minimum sable of continuous verified interaction time before gaining full weight. Enforcement: an identity's score decays unless it sustains activity, so factories must keep every identity warm simultaneously. Attacker cost is the orchard of parallel attention budgets—running thousands of identities for the summit window multiplies compute, scheduling, and monitoring spend, making mass registration economically irrational relative to honest single-identity use.
